brief: Why a 20-minute morning walk beat my $400 wearable.

slots.headline: Why Walks Beat Wearables?
slots.subtitle: I ditched the data and found something better outside.

slots.title: The Wearable Trap
slots.body: I chased sleep scores and recovery percentages for months. The $400 band promised optimization but delivered anxiety. More data didn't mean more health. It just meant more notifications.

slots.title: The Twenty-Minute Experiment
slots.body: I swapped the morning scroll for a walk around the block. No GPS, no heart rate zones, just pavement and daylight. Twenty minutes felt almost too simple to work.

slots.title: What Actually Changed
slots.body: My energy spiked before coffee. My mind felt quieter without a dashboard telling me I failed. Turns out, sunlight and movement are the oldest biohackers around.

slots.title: The Real Cost Breakdown
slots.body: The wearable cost four hundred dollars and required daily charging. The walk required shoes I already owned. One demanded attention; the other gave it back.

slots.title: Consistency Beats Intensity
slots.body: I missed the wearable when I forgot to charge it. I never missed a walk because the battery died. Simple rituals stick when the barrier to entry is just a front door.

slots.title: Start With A Walk
slots.body: You don't need another gadget to validate your health. You need twenty minutes of fresh air and a loop around your neighborhood. Sometimes the best tech is no tech at all.
